paragraphs.title: The Fire and the Rising of God's Glory

answers: A sapphire-like firmament and the likeness of a throne
easy.explanation: Ezekiel saw a firmament like a sapphire stone and the likeness of a throne above the cherubim.

answers: Coals of fire from between the cherubim
easy.explanation: He was commanded to take coals of fire from between the cherubim.
easy.q: What was the man clothed with linen commanded to take?

easy.explanation: The man was commanded to scatter the coals over the city.
easy.q: Where was the man told to scatter the coals?

medium.explanation: One cherub took fire from between the cherubim and put it into the man's hands.
medium.q: Who placed the fire into the hands of the man clothed with linen?

medium.explanation: The sound of their wings was heard even to the outer court.
medium.q: How far was the sound of the cherubim's wings heard?

answers: The entrance or doorway of a house
medium.explanation: A threshold is the sill or entrance at a doorway.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “threshold” refer to?

answers: It went up from the cherub and stood over the threshold
It stopped at the eastern gate
challenge.explanation: The glory first went up from the cherub and stood over the threshold of the house.
challenge.q: What happened first in the movement of the glory of the Lord?

answers: A cherub gave the fire to the man in linen
The cherubim hid the fire from the man
The fire consumed the cherubim's wings
challenge.explanation: One cherub stretched out his hand, took fire, and placed it into the man's hands.
challenge.q: What relationship between the cherubim and the fire is described?

answers: The voice of the Almighty God when he speaketh
The voice of a man whispering
challenge.explanation: The sound was compared to the voice of the Almighty God when he speaketh.
challenge.q: To what was the sound of the cherubim's wings compared?

easy.explanation: Ezekiel saw four wheels, one beside each cherub.
easy.q: How many wheels did Ezekiel see beside the cherubim?

answers: The colour of a beryl stone
easy.explanation: The wheels appeared like the colour of a beryl stone.
easy.q: What did the appearance of the wheels resemble?

easy.explanation: The wheels were full of eyes round about.
easy.q: What filled the wheels and their surrounding parts?

answers: They went upon their four sides and followed where the head looked
They moved only when the cherubim stood still
medium.explanation: The wheels went upon their four sides and followed the direction in which the head looked.
medium.q: How did the wheels move without turning?

medium.explanation: In Ezekiel's hearing, the wheels were called “O wheel.”
medium.q: What name was called to the wheels?

answers: Only one was full of eyes
medium.explanation: The four wheels had one likeness, as if one wheel were within another.
medium.q: What did the four wheels have in common?

answers: One wheel appeared to be within another
They were attached to the eastern gate
challenge.explanation: The appearance of a wheel within a wheel is connected with their movement upon their four sides.
challenge.q: What feature helps explain how the wheels could move in different directions?

answers: Their appearance was covered with eyes on every side
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that eyes surrounded the wheels and their parts.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the wheels being full of eyes round about?

answers: Human hands are seen, the wheels are described, and the wheels are named
The glory leaves the house, then the fire is scattered
The cherubim disappear, then the city is judged
challenge.explanation: First hands like a man's are seen under the wings, then the wheels are described, and finally they are called “O wheel.”
challenge.q: Which sequence of details appears in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Faces and Movement of the Cherubim

easy.q: How many faces did each cherub have?
How many wings did each cherub have?

answers: The living creature he saw by the river of Chebar
easy.explanation: Ezekiel identified them with the living creature he had seen by the river of Chebar.
easy.q: With what did Ezekiel identify the cherubim?

medium.explanation: The first face was the face of a cherub.
medium.q: What was the first face listed in the description?

answers: The wheels remained in the court
medium.explanation: When the cherubim went, the wheels went by them.
medium.q: What happened to the wheels when the cherubim went?

answers: The life or power within them
medium.explanation: The spirit of the living creature was in them and explains their coordinated movement.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “spirit” indicate about the living creatures?

answers: The wheels moved with the cherubim and did not turn away from them
The wheels always moved in the opposite direction
The wheels moved only after the cherubim stopped
challenge.explanation: The wheels went beside the cherubim and did not turn from beside them.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between the movement of the cherubim and the wheels?

answers: The wheels imitated the movement of the cherubim
The wheels determined the number of faces
challenge.explanation: When the cherubim stood, the wheels stood; when the cherubim rose, the wheels rose also.
challenge.q: What is meant by “when they stood, these stood”?

answers: The living creature seen there is identified as the cherubim
The same eastern gate is mentioned
The same man in linen is identified
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel says that the living creature he saw by the river of Chebar was the cherubim.
challenge.q: What link is made between this vision and the earlier vision by the river Chebar?

paragraphs.title: The Departure of God's Glory from the Temple

answers: From the threshold of the house
easy.explanation: The glory of the Lord departed from off the threshold of the house.
easy.q: From where did the glory of the Lord depart?

easy.explanation: The cherubim lifted up their wings and mounted up from the earth.
easy.q: Who lifted up their wings and rose from the earth?

answers: At the door of the east gate of the Lord's house
In the middle of the inner court
easy.explanation: They stood at the door of the east gate of the Lord's house.
easy.q: Where did the cherubim and wheels stand?

medium.explanation: The glory departed from the threshold and stood over the cherubim.
medium.q: Where did the glory of the Lord stand after leaving the threshold?

medium.explanation: When the cherubim went out, the wheels were beside them.
medium.q: What was beside the cherubim as they went out?

answers: The glory leaves the threshold and the cherubim stop at the eastern gate
The cloud enters the inner court
medium.explanation: The glory leaves the threshold, and the cherubim and wheels move to the eastern gate.
medium.q: Why does this passage describe movement outward from the house?

answers: The glory of the God of Israel
challenge.explanation: The glory of the God of Israel was over them above.
challenge.q: What was above the cherubim at the eastern gate?

answers: Their movement was shared and coordinated
The wheels remained on the earth
The cherubim were separate from the wheels
challenge.explanation: The cherubim rose from the earth, and the wheels were beside them as they went.
challenge.q: What does the cherubim and wheels rising together emphasize?

answers: From the threshold of the house to above the cherubim
From the eastern gate to the river only
From the wheel to the fire and then to the city
challenge.explanation: The glory leaves the threshold and stands over the cherubim.
challenge.q: What change in location of God's glory is described?

paragraphs.title: Identifying the Living Creatures as Cherubim

easy.explanation: Ezekiel knew that the living creature was the cherubim.
easy.q: With whom did Ezekiel identify the living creature he saw by the river Chebar?

easy.explanation: Every cherub had four faces apiece.
easy.q: How many faces did each cherub have?

answers: The likeness of the hands of a man
easy.explanation: The likeness of human hands was under their wings.
easy.q: What was under the wings of the cherubim?

answers: Their faces and appearances were the same
The living creatures had no wings
The cherubim had only human faces
medium.explanation: Ezekiel says their faces were the same faces he saw by the river of Chebar.
medium.q: What was the same about the faces of the cherubim and the living creatures by Chebar?

answers: Each went straight forward according to the direction of his face
They were carried by the cloud
medium.explanation: Each cherub went straight forward in the direction of his face.
medium.q: How did the cherubim move without turning aside?

answers: A form or appearance resembling human hands
A sound heard from far away
A place where the cherubim stood
medium.explanation: “Likeness” means a form or appearance resembling something.
medium.q: What does “likeness” mean in “the likeness of the hands of a man”?

answers: The creatures by the river Chebar are identified with the cherubim in the Temple vision
Only the fire is described in both passages
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel identifies the living creatures seen by Chebar as the cherubim.
challenge.q: What is the main connection between this passage and the beginning of the cherubim vision?

answers: Four faces, four wings, and human-like hands
Two faces, two wings, and angelic hands
One face, no wings, and no hands
challenge.explanation: The passage repeats that each cherub had four faces, four wings, and hands like a man's.
challenge.q: Which combination of features is repeated at the end of the chapter?

answers: Each cherub moved in the direction toward which his face was turned
The cherubim could move only in one shared direction
challenge.explanation: Their forward movement followed the direction of their faces.
challenge.q: What is explained by the statement that each went “straight forward”?
